source_refs.note: 3- Vectors: a main subheading of 20.2.1 Tools used in Recombinant DNA Technology, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 157-157.

blocks.text: Special molecules called vectors (or molecular carrier) are used for the introduction the of gene of interest into host cells. The gene of interest is attached to the vector and the vectors becomes a recombinant DNA (rDNA). Then, the rDNA is introduced into the host cells. The plasmids of bacteria are the most commonly used. Other vectors include;

blocks.alt: Source DNA with the gene of interest (pink) between two cut sites is cut by a restriction endonuclease into pieces with stepped ends, releasing the gene of interest. A ring-shaped vector (plasmid) is cut by the same enzyme into a cleaved vector. The gene of interest goes into the cleaved vector, and the two join into a ring of recombinant DNA.

items: Cosmids (plasmids that contain a small region of bacteriophage DNA called the cos sequence)
P1 artificial chromosomes (have features of both P1 vectors and Bacterial Artificial Chromosomes)

blocks.text: Animal viruses (e.g., human cold virus) also serve as vectors to carry genes of interest into monkey and human cells.
